seo.title: How to Build a Landing Page with Tailwind CSS | Conversion-Ready
seo.description: Build a high-converting landing page with Tailwind CSS featuring a hero section, features grid, testimonials, pricing, and CTA.

introduction: A well-designed landing page is the highest-ROI page on any website. Tailwind CSS lets you build one rapidly without switching between HTML and CSS files, and its utility-first approach makes responsive design straightforward. This guide builds a complete, conversion-optimized landing page with a hero section, features grid, social proof, pricing table, FAQ, and call-to-action — all fully responsive and production-ready.

prerequisites.name: Node.js 20+
prerequisites.description: Required for Tailwind CSS CLI and the Vite development server.

prerequisites.name: Basic HTML Knowledge
prerequisites.description: Understanding of semantic HTML elements, forms, and document structure.

prerequisites.name: A Text Editor
prerequisites.description: VS Code with the Tailwind CSS IntelliSense extension gives you autocomplete for every Tailwind class.

steps.title: Set Up the Project with Vite and Tailwind CSS
steps.description: Create a lightweight project using Vite as the development server and Tailwind CSS v4 for styling. Vite gives you instant hot module replacement, and Tailwind CSS v4 requires zero configuration — just import it in your CSS file. No tailwind.config.js needed.

code_snippet.code:
npm create vite@latest my-landing -- --template vanilla-ts
cd my-landing
npm install
npm install tailwindcss @tailwindcss/vite

# Update vite.config.ts to include the Tailwind plugin

tips: Tailwind CSS v4 uses a CSS-first configuration approach — customize your theme with @theme in your CSS file.
Install the Tailwind CSS IntelliSense extension in VS Code for class autocomplete and hover previews.

steps.title: Configure Tailwind CSS v4 with Custom Theme
steps.description: Set up your CSS file with Tailwind CSS v4 imports and define your custom theme using the @theme directive. Unlike v3, Tailwind v4 does not need a JavaScript config file. All theme customization happens in CSS, making it simpler and faster. Define your brand colors, fonts, and spacing scale.
tips: Use --color-brand consistently throughout the page for visual coherence.
Add Google Fonts in your HTML <head> for the custom font families defined in @theme.

steps.title: Build the Hero Section
steps.description: Create a compelling hero section with a headline, subheadline, call-to-action buttons, and a product screenshot or illustration. The hero is the first thing visitors see, so it must communicate your value proposition in under 5 seconds. Use Tailwind's responsive utilities for mobile-first design.

steps.title: Create the Features Grid
steps.description: Build a features section that highlights 3-6 key benefits of your product. Use a CSS grid that adapts from one column on mobile to three columns on desktop. Each feature card includes an icon, title, and description. Keep descriptions short — two sentences maximum.

tips: Use bg-brand/10 (10% opacity of brand color) for icon backgrounds to maintain visual consistency.
Keep feature descriptions to 1-2 sentences — visitors scan, they don't read.

steps.title: Add Social Proof with Testimonials
steps.description: Build a testimonial section with customer quotes, names, photos, and company logos. Social proof is one of the strongest conversion drivers on a landing page. Use a grid layout for multiple testimonials and highlight one featured testimonial with a larger card.

steps.title: Build the Pricing Table
steps.description: Create a pricing section with 2-3 tiers that makes the recommended plan visually prominent. The middle or most popular plan should be highlighted with a different background or border color. Include a feature comparison list and clear CTA buttons for each tier.

Keep pricing simple — too many tiers or add-ons confuse visitors and reduce conversions.

steps.title: Add the Final CTA and Footer
steps.description: Close the page with a strong call-to-action section that repeats your main value proposition and includes the primary conversion button. Follow it with a footer containing navigation links, social icons, and legal links. The final CTA captures visitors who have scrolled through the entire page and are ready to take action.

tips: Use a dark background for the final CTA to create visual contrast and draw attention.
The footer should repeat important links but not distract from the CTA above it.
Test the page on mobile — at least 60% of landing page traffic comes from mobile devices.

next_steps: Add scroll animations with CSS @keyframes or a lightweight library like Motion One.
Implement A/B testing on the headline and CTA copy using Vercel's Edge Config.
Connect a form to an email marketing tool like ConvertKit or Mailchimp for lead capture.
Optimize for Core Web Vitals by lazy-loading images below the fold and using font-display: swap.
